extracted.intended_audience: Patent applicants, patent agents, receiving Offices, designated Offices, and International Preliminary Examining Authorities handling PCT Chapter II demands and procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for filing and processing a Demand under PCT Chapter II (international preliminary examination), including restoration of priority, required documents, time limits, language and fee rules, and competent Authority procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of the right of priority — substantive criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an international application claims the priority of an earlier application and has an international filing date later than the date on which the priority period expired but within two months from that date, the designated Office shall, on the request of the applicant, restore the right of priority if the Office finds that a criterion applied by it is satisfied, namely, that the failure to file the international application within the priority period: (i) occurred in spite of due care required by the circumstances having been taken; or (ii) was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each designated Office shall apply at least one of those criteria and may apply both of them. (Rule 50(a))

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for restoration — filing, reasons, and supporting evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A request to restore the right of priority shall: (i) be filed with the designated Office within a time limit of one month from the applicable time limit under Article 22 or, where the applicant makes an express request to the designated Office under Article 23(2), within one month from the date of receipt of that request by the designated Office; (ii) state the reasons for the failure to file within the priority period and preferably be accompanied by any declaration or other evidence required; and (iii) be accompanied by any fee for requesting restoration required under paragraph (d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated Office may require declarations/evidence (Rule 50(c)) and may charge a fee for requesting restoration (Rule 50(d)). Failure to comply with procedural requirements may lead to refusal; applicant must be given opportunity to make observations prior to refusal (Rule 50(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated Office may require declaration or evidence for restoration
rubrics_metrics.description: The designated Office may require that a declaration or other evidence in support of the statement of reasons be filed with it within a time limit which shall be reasonable under the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time limit should be reasonable under the circumstances (no less specification here). This is separate from the one‑month filing requirement for the initial request. (Rule 50(c))

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated Office must give opportunity to comment before refusing restoration
rubrics_metrics.description: The designated Office shall not refuse, totally or in part, a request for restoration without giving the applicant the opportunity to make observations on the intended refusal within a time limit which shall be reasonable under the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such notice of intended refusal may be sent together with any invitation to file a declaration or other evidence under Rule 50(c). (Rule 50(e))

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated Office may apply more favorable national law for restoration
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the national law applicable by the designated Office provides, in respect of restoration of the right of priority, requirements more favorable to applicants than those in the PCT provisions, the designated Office may apply the national law instead of the PCT requirements when determining the right of priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each designated Office shall inform the International Bureau of which criterion(s) for restoration it applies and of any applicable national-law requirements and subsequent changes; the IB will publish such information in the Gazette. Transitional compatibility clause applies if paragraphs are not compatible with national law. (Rule 50(f)–(h))

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of altered time limits under Article 22(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Contracting State allowing a time limit expiring later than the time limits in Article 22(1) or (2) shall notify the International Bureau of the time limits so fixed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications received by the IB are promptly published in the Gazette. Shortenings of previously fixed time limits are effective only for international applications filed after three months from publication; lengthenings become effective upon publication (or later date if fixed by the Contracting State). (Rule 50.1(a)–(d))

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for presenting request to send copies (Rule 51.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limit referred to in Article 25(1)(c) shall be two months computed from the date of the notification sent to the applicant under Rule 20.4(i), 24.2(c) or 29.1(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the deadline for requesting the International Bureau to send file copies to Offices the applicant attempted to designate after a negative determination under Article 11(1). (Rule 51.1)

rubrics_metrics.name: Attach copy of notification when requesting file copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant, after a negative determination under Article 11(1), requests the International Bureau under Article 25(1) to send copies of the file of the purported international application to any named Offices he attempted to designate, he shall attach to his request a copy of the notification referred to in Rule 20.4(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Rule 51.2 / Rule 51bis)

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for paying national fee and furnishing translation (Rule 51.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limit referred to in Article 25(2)(a) shall expire at the same time as the time limit prescribed in Rule 51.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment of national fees and furnishing translations to designated Offices follow the same two‑month-from-notification timing as the request to send copies. (Rule 51.3)

rubrics_metrics.name: Certain national requirements that a designated Office may require — identity of inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: The national law applicable by the designated Office may require the applicant to furnish any document relating to the identity of the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to limits in Rule 51 bis.2 (i.e., Offices shall not require such documents if they reasonably rely on provided declarations). (Rule 51 bis.1(a)(i) and 51 bis.2(i))

rubrics_metrics.name: Certain national requirements that a designated Office may require — entitlement documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The national law applicable by the designated Office may require any document relating to the applicant’s entitlement to apply for or be granted a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes documents proving entitlement as of the international filing date; see Rule 51 bis.2(ii) for when such documents need not be required if a declaration is submitted. (Rule 51 bis.1(a)(ii) and 51 bis.2(ii))

rubrics_metrics.name: Certain national requirements that a designated Office may require — proof of entitlement to claim priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The national law applicable by the designated Office may require any document containing proof of the applicant’s entitlement to claim priority of an earlier application where the applicant is not the applicant who filed the earlier application or where the applicant’s name has changed since the earlier application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A declaration under Rule 4.17(iii) may obviate the need to require documentary proof (see Rule 51 bis.2(iii)). (Rule 51 bis.1(a)(iii))

rubrics_metrics.name: Certain national requirements that a designated Office may require — oath or declaration of inventorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the international application designates a State whose national law requires (on Oct 9, 2012) the furnishing of an oath or declaration of inventorship, the national law may require any document containing an oath or declaration of inventorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a declaration of inventorship as per Rule 4.17(iv) is contained in the request or submitted directly, the Office shall not require the document unless it reasonably doubts veracity. (Rule 51 bis.1(a)(iv) and 51 bis.2(iv))

rubrics_metrics.name: Certain national requirements that a designated Office may require — evidence concerning non-prejudicial disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The national law applicable may require any evidence concerning non-prejudicial disclosures or exceptions to lack of novelty, such as disclosures resulting from abuse, disclosures at certain exhibitions and disclosures by the applicant during a certain period of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such evidence may be required under Article 27 as implemented by national law. (Rule 51 bis.1(a)(v))

rubrics_metrics.name: Certain national requirements that a designated Office may require — confirmation by signature
rubrics_metrics.description: The national law applicable may require the confirmation of the international application by the signature of any applicant for the designated State who has not signed the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may be applied where national law requires applicant signatures for national processing. (Rule 51 bis.1(a)(vi))

rubrics_metrics.name: Certain national requirements that a designated Office may require — missing applicant indications
rubrics_metrics.description: The national law applicable may require any missing indication required under Rule 4.5(a)(ii) and (iii) in respect of any applicant for the designated State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated Offices may insist on completion of missing applicant information per their national requirements. (Rule 51 bis.1(a)(vii))

rubrics_metrics.name: Certain national requirements that a designated Office may require — translations of erroneously filed elements
rubrics_metrics.description: In the cases referred to in Rule 82 ter.1, a translation of any erroneously filed element or part removed from the international application in accordance with Rule 20.5 bis(b) or (c) may be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied when national law authorizes requiring translations of elements removed at the international stage for national processing. (Rule 51 bis.1(a)(viii))

rubrics_metrics.name: National law may require representation and appointment of agent
rubrics_metrics.description: The national law applicable by the designated Office may require that the applicant be represented by an agent having the right to represent applicants before that Office and/or have an address in the designated State for the purpose of receiving notifications, and that the agent, if any, be duly appointed by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is permitted under Article 27(6) or (7) and implemented via Rule 51 bis.1(b). (Rule 51 bis.1(b))

rubrics_metrics.name: National law may require multiple copies
rubrics_metrics.description: The national law applicable by the designated Office may require that the international application, the translation thereof or any document relating thereto be furnished in more than one copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is permitted under Article 27(1) as implemented by Rule 51 bis.1(c). (Rule 51 bis.1(c))

rubrics_metrics.name: National law may require verification or certification of translations
rubrics_metrics.description: The national law may require that the translation of the international application furnished by the applicant be: (i) verified by the applicant or the person having translated it in a statement that the translation is complete and faithful; or (ii) certified by a public authority or sworn translator, but only where the designated Office may reasonably doubt the accuracy of the translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verification is a declaration by translator/applicant; certification by public authority only where reasonable doubt exists. (Rule 51 bis.1(d))

rubrics_metrics.name: National law may require translation of priority document under limited circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: The national law applicable may require the applicant to furnish a translation of the priority document, provided that such a translation may only be required: (i) where the validity of the priority claim is relevant to determining patentability; or (ii) where the international filing date was accorded on the basis of incorporation by reference of an element or part, and for determining under Rule 82 ter.1(b) whether that element or part is completely contained in the priority document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a part of the description, claims or drawings is involved, the Office may also require an indication of where that part is contained in the translation of the priority document. (Rule 51 bis.1(e) and 51 bis.1(e)(ii))

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances in which documents/evidence may not be required
rubrics_metrics.description: The designated Office shall not, unless it may reasonably doubt the veracity of the indications or declaration concerned, require any document or evidence relating to: (i) identity of the inventor (other than an oath/declaration if required); (ii) applicant’s entitlement to apply for/be granted a patent; (iii) applicant’s entitlement to claim priority; or (iv) an oath or declaration of inventorship, if appropriate declarations are contained in or submitted with the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows Offices to rely on Rule 4.17 declarations instead of documentary proof unless reasonable doubt exists. (Rule 51 bis.2(i)–(iv))

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to comply with national requirements — invitation and time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a national requirement is not already fulfilled during the same period within which Article 22 requirements must be complied with, the designated Office shall invite the applicant to comply within a time limit which shall not be less than two months from the date of the invitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each designated Office may require the applicant to pay a fee for complying with national requirements in response to the invitation. For some national-law requirements (Article 27(6) or (7)) the applicant may have opportunity to comply after the expiration of that period. (Rule 51 bis.3(a)–(b))

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit to exercise right under Article 28 (amendments before designated Offices)
rubrics_metrics.description: In any designated State in which processing or examination starts without special request, the applicant shall, if he so wishes, exercise the right under Article 28 within one month from the fulfillment of the requirements under Article 22; provided that if communication under Rule 47.1 has not been effected by the expiration of the time limit applicable under Article 22, he shall exercise the right not later than four months after such expiration date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may exercise the right at any later time if permitted by the national law of that State. (Rule 52.1(a))

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of the Demand — printed form or computer printout
rubrics_metrics.description: The demand shall be made on a printed form or be presented as a computer print out. The particulars of the printed form and of a demand presented as a computer print out shall be prescribed by the Administrative Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of printed demand forms shall be furnished free of charge by the receiving Office or by the International Preliminary Examining Authority. (Rule 53.1(a)–(b))

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the Demand — petition and indications
rubrics_metrics.description: The demand shall contain: (i) a petition; (ii) indications concerning the applicant and the agent if there is an agent; (iii) indications concerning the international application to which it relates; and where applicable, a statement concerning amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested wording for the petition is provided in the Rule. Identification of the international application must include applicant name and address, title of the invention, international filing date (if known) and international application number or, if unknown, the name of the receiving Office. (Rules 53.2 and 53.6)

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirement for the Demand
rubrics_metrics.description: The demand shall be signed. The demand shall be signed by the applicant or, if more than one applicant, by all applicants making the demand (but see Rule 60(a‑ter) regarding sufficiency of signature by one of multiple applicants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signature formalizes the demand; exceptions allow one applicant's signature in certain multi‑applicant cases. (Rule 53.8 and Rule 60(a‑ter))

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement concerning amendments in the Demand
rubrics_metrics.description: If amendments under Article 19 have been made, the statement concerning amendments shall indicate whether, for international preliminary examination, the applicant wishes those amendments: (i) to be taken into account (preferably submit copy of amendments and required letter with demand); or (ii) to be considered as reversed by an amendment under Article 34. If no Article 19 amendments have been made and the time limit for filing such amendments has not expired, the statement may indicate that the applicant wishes postponement of the start of the international preliminary examination so it can start at the same time as the international search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any Article 34 amendments are submitted with the demand, the statement must indicate that. If the demand states Article 34 amendments are submitted but none are, the Authority shall invite the applicant to submit them and proceed under Rule 69.1(e). (Rule 53.9 and Rule 60(g))

rubrics_metrics.name: Who is entitled to make a Demand — residence/nationality and filing Office
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to make a demand exists if the applicant making the demand (or at least one of multiple applicants) is a resident or national of a Contracting State bound by Chapter II and the international application has been filed with a receiving Office of or acting for a Contracting State bound by Chapter II. Residence/nationality is determined according to Rule 18.1(a) and (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where there is doubt, the International Preliminary Examining Authority shall request the receiving Office or national Office to decide and shall inform the applicant, who may submit arguments. If the applicant does not have the right to make a demand, the demand shall be considered not to have been submitted. (Rules 54.1–54.4)

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for making a Demand (Rule 54 bis.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A demand may be made at any time prior to the expiration of whichever of the following periods expires later: (i) three months from the date of transmittal to the applicant of the international search report or the declaration referred to in Article 17(2)(a), and of the written opinion established under Rule 43 bis.1; or (ii) 22 months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any demand made after that time limit shall be considered as if it had not been submitted. (Rule 54 bis.1(a)–(b))

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of the Demand and translations (Rule 55.1–55.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The demand shall be in the language of the international application or, if the international application has been filed in a language other than the language in which it is published, in the language of publication. However, if a translation of the international application is required under Rule 55.2, the demand shall be in the language of that translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If neither the filing nor publication language is accepted by the IPEA, the applicant must furnish a translation into a language accepted by the Authority and a language of publication. Translation must include specified elements and parts (Article 11(1)(iii)(d)/(e) and parts considered contained under Rule 20.6(b)). The IPEA shall check the translation for compliance with physical requirements to the extent necessary. If a translation was transmitted to the ISA and the IPEA is part of the same Office, applicant need not furnish it again. If translation or required language materials are missing or non‑compliant, the IPEA shall invite the applicant to furnish them within a reasonable time (not less than one month); failure leads to the demand being considered not submitted or amendments not taken into account as specified. Amendments and certain letters must be submitted in language of publication or of the required translation. (Rule 55.1–55.3)

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling fee requirement and payment timing (Rule 57)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each demand for international preliminary examination shall be subject to payment of a handling fee for the benefit of the International Bureau, to be collected by the International Preliminary Examining Authority to which the demand is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handling fee shall be paid within one month from the date the demand was submitted or 22 months from the priority date, whichever expires later (subject to exceptions where transmitted under Rule 59.3 or where IPEA invites payment to start exam with search). Amount payable is the amount applicable on the date of payment. Refunds are required if the demand is withdrawn before being sent to the IB or if the demand is considered not submitted. Currency conversion and transfer rules for payment to the IB are specified. (Rule 57.1–57.4)

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary examination fee (Rule 58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each International Preliminary Examining Authority may require that the applicant pay a 'preliminary examination fee' for its own benefit for carrying out the international preliminary examination and performing related tasks. The amount, time limit for payment and amount payable follow Rule 57.3 mutatis mutandis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fee is payable directly to the IPEA in the currency prescribed by that Office; IPEAs shall inform the IB of the extent/conditions under which they will refund amounts paid where the demand is considered not submitted. (Rule 58.1, 58.3)

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension/invitation to pay insufficient fees (Rule 58 bis.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the IPEA finds that the amount paid is insufficient to cover the handling fee and the preliminary examination fee, or that no fees were paid by the time they are due, the Authority shall invite the applicant to pay the amount required, together with any late payment fee, within a time limit of one month from the date of the invitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant fails to pay within that time limit the demand shall, subject to paragraph (c), be considered as if it had not been submitted and the IPEA shall so declare. Any payment received before the invitation is considered to have been received before expiration of the original time limit. (Rule 58 bis.1)

rubrics_metrics.name: Late payment fee calculation (Rule 58 bis.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The payment of fees in response to an invitation for insufficient payment may be subjected to a late payment fee equal to: (i) 50% of the amount of unpaid fees specified in the invitation; or (ii) if that amount is less than the handling fee, an amount equal to the handling fee. The late payment fee shall not exceed double the amount of the handling fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This caps the penalty for late/insufficient payment and sets minimums. (Rule 58 bis.2)

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent International Preliminary Examining Authority designation and publication (Rule 59.1–59.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For demands under Article 31(2)(a), each receiving Office shall inform the International Bureau which IPEA(s) are competent for international preliminary examination of applications filed with it; the IB shall publish such information. Where several IPEAs are competent, provisions of Rule 35.2 apply mutatis mutandis. For demands under Article 31(2)(b), the Assembly shall give preference to the IPEA of the national Office which is an IPEA, or to the IPEA recommended by that Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures transparency about which Authorities are competent; applicant may be given choice where multiple competent IPEAs exist. (Rule 59.1–59.2)

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal of the Demand to the competent IPEA (Rule 59.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the demand is submitted to an Office/Authority not competent, that Office shall mark the date of receipt and transmit the demand promptly to the International Bureau (unless it decides to transmit directly to a competent IPEA). The IB shall promptly transmit the demand to the competent IPEA if only one exists or invite the applicant to choose among competent IPEAs where two or more exist; failure to indicate results in the demand being considered not submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A demand transmitted to a competent IPEA is considered received on the date marked on it when first received by the initial Office/IB. If an Office/Authority directly transmits to the competent IPEA, the same transmittal/date rules apply. (Rule 59.3(a)–(f))

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of defects in the Demand (Rule 60.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the demand does not comply with requirements in Rules 53.1, 53.2(a)(i)–(iii), 53.2(b), 53.3–53.8 and 55.1, the IPEA shall invite the applicant to correct the defects within a reasonable time limit, which shall not be less than one month from the date of the invitation (may be extended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant complies within the time limit, the demand is considered as received on the actual filing date provided identification was possible; otherwise the demand is considered received on the date of correction. Failure to comply results in the demand being treated as not submitted. Special rules: where multiple applicants, certain indications/signatures by one applicant suffice (Rule 60(a‑bis),(a‑ter)). If defect noticed by the IB, IB brings it to IPEA's attention. If the demand lacks a statement concerning amendments, IPEA proceeds under Rules 66.1 and 69.1(a)/(b). If the statement indicates Article 34 amendments but none were submitted, the IPEA shall invite the applicant to submit them within a fixed time and proceed under Rule 69.1(e). (Rule 60.1 and related paragraphs)
